transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Harper (StratoGrid Head of Solutions), Omar Khan (StratoGrid Platform Eng), Priya Menon (StratoGrid Security)
Meeting purpose: technical alignment for marketplace listing, edge caching pattern, and governance/onboarding playbook for joint solution.

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Reviewed StratoGrid's network and where Redwood runtime will sit (edge cache patterns, cluster topology).
- Discussed marketplace packaging (helm operator vs chart, operator versioning), listing metadata, and billing tags.
- Went over KMS / SSO and audit-log requirements; clarified SOC2 artifacts and RBAC model.
- Agreed pilot benchmarks, next steps for on-prem pilot kickoff and a document handoff schedule.

Topics:
- Edge cache TTL / prefix caching behavior
- VPC peering, private control plane, and egress rules
- Marketplace operator packaging & helm chart CI
- KMS, HSM compatibility and logging retention
- Quantization options for ARM/INT8 on edge GPUs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to kick off the deep technical sync on the StratoGrid joint offering, um — quick round of intros?
[00:08] Lena: hey all, Lena here, I run solutions at StratoGrid. Omar and Priya are on for platform and security.
[00:13] Omar: hi, thanks. we've been doing some early integration tests, mostly with your hosted api, but now we want the marketplace listing and also the on-prem/edge operator flow.
[00:22] Diego: great, great. quick spoiler, we brought some performance notes and a proposed canary pattern for edge caches.
[00:27] Priya: quick note from security: we need to make sure SSO, SAML, and per-tenant KMS keys line up; also audit logs retention needs to be 1 year minimum for our customers.
[00:37] Maya: yep, noted. agenda: 1) deployment topologies, 2) packaging and listing checklist, 3) security/keys and logging, 4) performance and quant options, 5) next steps. anything to add?
[00:47] Lena: no, let's go.

[00:55] Diego: starting topology: we typically propose two patterns for partners — operator-based install (helm + operator) for air-gapped or on-prem, and a lightweight connector + managed nodes for marketplace 'hosted' listings. For StratoGrid at edge locations I think operator is better because you manage lifecycle.
[01:12] Omar: operator is preferable, yes. we also run a fleet of k8s clusters on the edge, some are 1-3 node clusters with M60-like GPUs, others are larger. how does Redwood handle prefix caching across small clusters?
[01:28] Diego: good question. our runtime supports prefix/KV cache that can be local or shared. on tiny clusters we push smaller kv shards and rely on nearest-node caching. there's tradeoffs — more local cache reduces cross-node latency but reduces hit rate if requests are dispersed.
[01:45] Omar: ok that makes sense, can you quantify hit rates?  we have bursty traffic on morning windows.
[01:52] Diego: rough numbers — if you shard by region and have sticky routing, hit rates go up to 65-80% for repeated prefixes within a 5-10 minute window. if traffic is uniformly random across thousands of users, hit goes down to 30-40. these are ballpark for our default batcher and 8k seq lengths.
[02:12] Lena: is that affected by quantization? i.e., if we move to int8 to save memory, does cache behavior change?
[02:18] Diego: not really for the KV structure, but quantization changes kernel choices and latency per token. int8 can reduce mem by ~4x and CPU/GPU time by 20-40% depending on hw. but we saw slightly different warmup characteristics; so initial tokens might be marginally slower until caches warm.

[02:40] Maya: let's park that and talk packaging — listing metadata. StratoGrid, for marketplace we need a listing that includes: operator chart, quickstart, network prerequisites, and a reference arch doc. our listing team also wants an explicit 'supported topologies' table.
[02:56] Omar: supported topologies: single-node edge heavy inference, multi-node pooled inference, and hybrid with Redwood Dedicated fallover. We'll send a doc later.
[03:06] Diego: the operator will include pre-set RBAC roles, a CRD to pin model version and rollout policy, and hooks for canary traffic (we can add Istio/ingress hints).
[03:17] Priya: on RBAC — do you support granular audit logs, like per-route token-level logging? we need to be able to show which token used which model and which customer data touched the request.
[03:27] Diego: yes, we emit token-level usage logs with model_id, route, and request metadata. one caveat: PII in logs — we recommend scrubbing or tokenizing sensitive fields before logging.
[03:36] Priya: great. and KMS? we need to know whether you allow customer-managed KMS per cluster.
[03:41] Maya: yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via a key-mount shim; for marketplace operator installs we can support a K8s secret that is a reference to the customer KMS, or an external KMS connector.
[03:54] Omar: sounds good. for air-gapped installs we can't reach outside KMS, so how does rotation and envelope encryption work?
[04:01] Diego: for air-gapped we ship a short-running local KMS shim that talks to an HSM inside your network, and keys are rotated by your ops team per policy. we also provide an offline key import tool.

[04:15] Lena: let's dig into the logging retention and export. we need to send audit logs to our SIEM for 1 year. is that supported or do you require us to pull?
[04:25] Maya: both — we can ship logs to an external endpoint via fluentd/otlp. retention is configurable; marketplace listing will include recommended retention settings and a retention playbook.

[04:40] Diego: switching to performance — we propose a pilot with two benchmarks: 1) latency p95 for 512-token seq at 100rps steady; 2) sustained throughput test at 1k req/min with variable seq lengths and reply sizes. we can run these on your smallest edge node and on a larger pool for comparison.
[04:58] Omar: can you run this on our p3-ish fleet and on arm-accelerated nodes? we have some Jetson/arm devices in edge lab.
[05:06] Diego: yes, we support CUDA GPUs and have experimental arm builds for T4-ish and specialized accelerators. quantization matters: int8 on arm often needs different kernels and may not be as optimized as x86.
[05:18] Priya: if we publish a marketplace listing that says 'arm supported' we need tests and a compatibility badge.
[05:24] Maya: agreed — we can do a compatibility badge but it requires a joint validation run and a small certification checklist.

[05:36] [06:00] Speaker 6 (transcription hiccup: might be Diego): sorry, background noise.

[05:58] Diego: no worries. on deployment patterns for the operator we want to provide two modes: managed control-plane (Redwood private control plane in VPC with a connector) and fully private (control plane in StratoGrid). marketplace listing should show both options.
[06:12] Omar: for fully private, what's the upgrade path? we have strict change windows and need rolling upgrades without losing warm KV caches.
[06:22] Diego: rolling upgrades keep KV metadata, but cache warmup is an operational cost. we have a graceful handoff where we migrate live suffixes to new pods gradually; there will likely be a temporary QPS dip. Canary with traffic mirroring reduces impact.

[06:38] Lena: about billing and metering: when customer deploys from marketplace, how do we meter usage for Redwood billing? we prefer a metering connector that emits usage events back to Redwood for billing reconciliation.
[06:50] Maya: marketplace flows can be either license-based (StratoGrid bills and credits Redwood) or a revenue-sharing metered model. Technical side: operator will include a metering sidecar that aggregates per-tenant usage and sends batched events over mTLS.
[07:04] Omar: ok, sidecar must be configurable to avoid sending sensitive PII.

[07:12] Diego: also worth noting, for burst capacity we support an autoscale-to-dedicated policy that routes overflow to Redwood Dedicated zones — useful if you want predictable SLA during peaks. We'll document routing policy in the ref arch.
[07:25] Priya: on compliance: can you provide SOC2 Type II and pen test reports in NDA? that's required for our enterprise customers.
[07:32] Maya: yes, we'll share the SOC2 package under our customer NDA; I'll attach it to the listing packet.

[07:42] [08:00] Maya: quick checkpoint — we've covered topology, packaging, security, perf. Now Diego will walk through the proposed canary traffic flow and an example helm chart structure. Diego?

[08:10] Diego: slide-free walkthru. operator CRD: ModelDeployment with fields: model_version, rollout_strategy (canary/bluegreen), traffic_split, cache_policy (ttl, shard_strategy), and kms_ref. The operator will write status to a ConfigMap and expose metrics via Prometheus.
[08:28] Omar: will those status fields be namespaced per-tenant?
[08:32] Diego: yes, CRD is namespaced. metrics include model_id, pod_latency_ms, kv_hit_rate, and batch_size. We'll keep the schema stable across minor versions but allow experimental flags.

[08:45] Lena: about schema stability — marketplace customers dislike breaking changes. what's your semver for the operator?
[08:51] Diego: operator follows semver with deprecation cycles: major bump for breaking changes with 6-month notice. We'll publish migration guides.

[09:00] Priya: a question on network policies: can the operator lock egress and only allow particular endpoints for metering/billing? we need a hard allowlist.
[09:09] Diego: yes, you can configure egress to only the Redwood endpoints; metering is batched to a single mTLS endpoint and we provide IP ranges and DNS names. For air-gapped instances, metering can be stored and shipped by hand.

[09:24] Maya: let's call out the docs we'll hand over for the listing: install guide, upgrade guide, network whitelist, KMS integration guide, SOC2 package pointer, operator reference CRD, and a quickstart helm chart. We'll produce a checklist for the marketplace portal.

[09:40] Omar: timeline — we want a listing live by end of Q1 2026. Does that feel doable?
[09:46] Maya: yes, with a pilot in Dec and Jan we can target a Feb listing and a public GA end of Q1.

[09:55] Diego: quick technical risk list: 1) arm quant kernel parity 2) KV cache warmup for micro clusters 3) operator upgrades in windows 4) billing connector privacy. We'll propose mitigations in the ref arch doc.

[10:15] Lena: can we get a short matrix comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private for StratoGrid use-cases? we want simple guidance for sales.
[10:22] Maya: yes, we'll include a one-pager in the listing packet.

[10:30] [10:45] Diego: demo note — I can spin up a small p3 instance and run a 30-minute sustained workload and share logs/results; will need SSH and k8s access or we can use a repo-and-script model.

[10:50] Omar: repo-and-script would be easier for us. please post it to the joint repo.
[10:54] Diego: will do.

[11:00] Priya: about certs — do you support kube-native cert manager integration for cert rotation?
[11:06] Diego: yes, cert-manager is supported; we'll include a how-to in the install guide.

[11:12] Maya: ok real quick, let's set success criteria for the pilot:
- technical: p95 latency under 600ms for 512-token on edge node in 80% of runs
- stability: no operator crashes in 72-hour soak
- security: KMS integration validated and SOC2 artifacts provided to StratoGrid
- listing: marketplace entry QA pass and docs uploaded

[11:40] Lena: sounds good.

[11:44] Diego: small nit — for the latency metric we need to agree on what counts as the request: include network egress to Redwood fallback or not? my suggestion: two labels, local-only and local-with-fallback.
[11:56] Omar: agreed. we'll use local-only for baseline.

[12:02] Maya: ok next steps recap: Maya send listing draft + pricing matrix; Diego run bench + push repo script; Omar share network topology; Priya gather SOC2 artefacts. schedule pilot kickoff week of 12/15.

[12:18] [12:35] Speaker 2 (background): thanks all.

[12:25] Lena: one more question — does Redwood have an official operator image that we can scan?
[12:30] Diego: yes, images are published to our registry with digests and SBOMs. we'll include SBOM and CVE scan results in the listing doc.

[12:40] Priya: perfect. thanks everyone.

[12:43] Maya: great, thanks — we'll follow up in email and attach the SOC2 NDA pack. Diego and I will make the bench plan and listing skeleton and post to the joint repo.

[12:50] Lena: thanks, bye.

End transcript.
